title: Certified Commitment Horizons in Dynamic Lot Sizing: Exact Prefix Stability, Optimal-Face Witnesses and One-Step Forecast Calibration
shortTitle: Certified commitment horizons in dynamic lot sizing
oneLine: An exact-rational candidate separates an abstract forced-source path model from its classical lot-sizing interpretation, then certifies how far forecast demand may move before a protected setup prefix can cease to be compulsory among optimal plans.
abstract: This anonymous, unrefereed theoretical-computational candidate studies weighted commitment radii for prefix stability in dynamic lot sizing. Version 3.0.0 repairs the semantic bridge between the forced-source affine path model and ordinary uncapacitated Wagner–Whitin setup schedules: the classical interpretation is made only under explicit active-horizon conditions. Within that scope, the manuscript gives exact floor-aware fixed-path tie distances, a polynomial frozen-comparator lower certificate, certified lower–upper brackets, a prefix-to-arc decomposition, a single-detour optimal-face theorem, exact-rational software and bounded finite audits. It also gives one-step marginal conformal calibration under exchangeability and a deterministic structural-loss bound under uncapacitated quantity recourse. Producer replay, CI and internal editorial review pass; independent reproduction, proof-assistant verification, external specialist review, journal peer review, exhaustive novelty and operational validation have not occurred.
narration: This anonymous, unrefereed research release asks a planning question: when demand forecasts change, how much movement can a production plan tolerate before its near-term setup decisions may need to change? The candidate studies this through a weighted commitment radius. Informally, the radius measures the nearest admissible forecast revision at which an optimal revised plan can stop sharing a protected prefix with the nominal plan. Version three makes an important repair. The software’s basic object is a forced-source path graph in which every complete path begins at period one. That graph does not always equal the ordinary physical lot-sizing model. If first-period demand can be zero, an ordinary plan may wait before opening a setup, while the forced-source graph still charges the first node. The release therefore uses a classical active-horizon interpretation only when the first-period demand floor is strictly positive and later setup costs are strictly positive, alongside the stated ordered-slope, inventory and no-backlogging assumptions. A leading-zero-demand counterexample is retained as a negative control. Within the declared model, the paper derives the exact floor-aware distance to a tie with any fixed competing path. It constructs a prefix-deviation graph, proves a polynomial exact-rational frozen-comparator lower certificate, and combines lower and upper witnesses into certified brackets. The familiar three-period example still has frozen radius three halves and exact strong radius two, showing that the lower certificate can be conservative. New structural results decompose a multi-arc protected prefix into one-arc suffix problems and show that every finite nearest loss has adjacent co-optimal inside and outside paths differing on a single divergence-and-remergence interval. The release also distinguishes exact values, certified intervals, guarded refusals and solver-level results instead of collapsing them into one answer. Its evidence includes ninety-four deterministic tests, three hundred twenty exact semantic-bridge comparisons, three hundred thirty brute-force certification comparisons, two hundred fifty-four finite optimal-face witnesses, exact-rational records, a separately implemented producer-side checker, fresh-extraction replay and CI on Python three point eleven and three point thirteen, both normally and with assertions disabled. The statistical layer offers one-step marginal conformal coverage only under exchangeability; it is not adaptive or time-uniform. The UCI case uses reconstructed forecast vintages and stylised costs, so it is an interface illustration, not evidence of industrial savings or field validity. GitHub and Zenodo expose matching public assets. Those facts establish availability and producer-side replay, not independent reproduction, formal verification, external specialist review, peer review, priority or impact. For reviewers, the highest-value next step is not another run of the same code. It is a clean-room reconstruction of the semantic bridge, fixed-path distance, prefix-deviation graph and single-detour argument, followed by an independent operations-research reading. A future operational study would need genuine forecast vintages, actual setup and holding costs, capacity and service constraints, a predeclared comparator, and outcomes collected prospectively. Until those gates are crossed, the release should be used as an auditable candidate method and research object, not as a validated production-planning policy. This synthetic-voice briefing is a communication aid. The paper, exact archive, verification receipt and open assurance gates are linked on the Evidence Press page.

keyResults: The release separates forced_source_graph semantics from a classical_active_horizon interpretation and proves sufficient bridge conditions, with a leading-zero-demand negative control.
For a fixed competing path, the candidate gives an exact floor-aware weighted-L-infinity distance to a cost tie.
A prefix-deviation DAG gives a polynomial exact-rational frozen-comparator lower certificate and a certified lower–upper bracket; the partial-prefix certificate can be strict.
A protected k-arc prefix decomposes into at most k one-arc suffix radii, and every finite nearest loss admits a single-detour adjacent optimal-face witness.
The interface preserves exact, interval, refusal and solver-level states; its one-step calibration theorem is marginal and conditional on exchangeability.
evidence: The public v3 package contains the 40-page manuscript, accessible documentation, source code, version-matched wheel, exact-rational certificates and witnesses, a separately implemented producer-side record checker, 94 deterministic tests, ordinary and optimized replay, semantic and mutation controls, raw and processed audit tables, a pinned environment, fresh-extraction evidence, PDF preflight, SHA-256 manifest, machine-readable claims and assurance records, five journal-like internal role reports plus confirmation and licensing-closure reports, and a final verification receipt. Finite ledgers include 320 exact semantic-bridge matches, 330 brute-force certification comparisons, 254 finite optimal-face witnesses, 512 bracket rows and 627 stratified compact-model rows. Python 3.11 and 3.13 GitHub Actions passed, and GitHub and Zenodo assets matched after unauthenticated download. These are producer-side and CI checks, not universal machine proofs, independent reproduction, formal verification, external review or field validation.
statusDetail: Anonymous, unrefereed theoretical-computational candidate. Exact release verification, fresh extraction, manifest coverage, 94 ordinary and optimized tests, Python 3.11/3.13 CI, bounded finite audits, internal five-role editorial review and byte-identical GitHub/Zenodo readback pass. Universal theorem claims still rest on manuscript proofs. No unaffiliated rerun, independently authored implementation, proof-assistant formalization, external operations-research specialist review, journal peer review, exhaustive priority audit or prospective operating-supply-chain evaluation is reported. The classical interpretation is limited to the stated active-horizon bridge; the UCI exercise is illustrative and does not establish benefit.
